name: Loss aversion

evidence.basis: Prospect theory (Kahneman & Tversky 1979); Nobel Prize 2002; cross-cultural replications over 45 years
evidence.effect_size_note: Losses weigh ~1.8–2.25x equivalent gains; weakens on small stakes

pinned_evidence.title: On the Descriptive Value of Loss Aversion in Decisions under Risk
pinned_evidence.reason: small-stakes boundary condition, cited in dossier

pinned_evidence.title: How to Make Loss Aversion Disappear and Reverse
pinned_evidence.reason: context-dependence boundary condition, cited in dossier

mechanism_summary_for_context: A loss is experienced ~2x more intensely than an equivalent gain. Users are more strongly motivated NOT TO LOSE what they have accumulated (streak, projects, status, discount) than to gain something new. 'Keep / don't lose' framing outperforms 'get / buy' framing.

preconditions.reason: you cannot lose what you do not have; blocked for brand-new users

applicability.culture_note: The mechanism is universal; what varies culturally is WHAT is valuable to lose (status vs. savings vs. time)

implementations.generation_directive: Frame the user's recurring action as a streak with a visible counter. Push/widget triggers on the RISK of the streak resetting; framing is preservation ('Don't lose your 12 days'), not achievement.
copy_formulas: {n} days in a row — {h} hours left to keep it going

implementations.generation_directive: The paywall shows what the user has CREATED (previews of their projects/results) and frames payment as keeping access to what is theirs, not as a purchase. State a concrete number and deadline: 'Your {n} projects will be deleted in {d} days'.
copy_formulas: Your {n} projects will be deleted in {d} days

implementations.generation_directive: The cancellation screen lists the user's concrete accumulated value (history, status, discount, created objects) with numbers. Neutral tone, no pleading, no shame. Cancel and keep buttons are equally visible.
copy_formulas: If you cancel, you will lose: {value_items}

implementations.generation_directive: Reminder that accumulated value expires, with a concrete date and amount. Frequency ≤ 2 touches per expiry cycle.
Where a benefit exists, frame it as loss prevention: 'Stop losing ${x}/month' instead of 'Save ${x}/month'. Apply selectively — no more than 1 loss frame per screen.

hard_rules.rule: The loss must be real; fake discounts and fake timers are forbidden
Buttons that shame refusal ('No, I want to pay more') are forbidden
Deleting user data is never used as pressure; genuine deletion requires ≥30-day notice and export
When accumulated_value_score = 0, the mechanism is not applied

constraints.boundary_test: If the user learned exactly how this works, would they shrug — or feel deceived?

relations.note: Endowment creates the value that LA-01 protects. Sequence: EN-03 → LA-01
Incompleteness is an adjacent tension, a different mechanism

reference_examples.what: Streak as the retention core; fear of losing the streak drives daily return; Streak Freeze monetizes the fear directly
Cancellation flow enumerates concrete owned benefits that disappear, turning a subscription expense into property
Expiring stars trigger visits: customers come to rescue what is theirs, not to buy coffee
